title: Your Employees Are Creating Content. Your Legal Department Should Be Paying Attention.
tldr: As employee-generated content becomes a core brand channel, legal risk and governance gaps are surfacing. A timely reminder that EGC needs guardrails, not just enthusiasm.
why_fresh: EGC governance angle rarely covered from legal lens
angle: A content governance framework for scaling employee-generated content without legal landmines.

title: Five takeaways from the Future of Media Technology Conference: How publishers are rethinking audience engagement
tldr: Reuters Institute distills how publishers are reworking audience engagement strategies amid AI disruption. Concrete signals on how media consumption is shifting.
why_fresh: fresh conference insights on consumption shifts
angle: What publishers' engagement pivots teach brand content teams about earning attention.

title: The Only Two Types of Content that AI Can Never Make
tldr: Argues that first-hand experience and original research are the two content types AI can't replicate — the human moat for creators. A useful frame for human-centered content strategy.
angle: Building a content strategy around what only humans can make in an AI-flooded feed.

title: Dentsu taps microdrama trend for Co-op
tldr: Co-op launches its first microdrama, prompting the question of whether it's a genuinely new format or a relabelling of branded short video. A concrete campaign breakdown of an emerging format.
angle: Is 'microdrama' a real new format or repackaged branded content? A skeptic's breakdown.

title: AI Traffic Conversion Rates: New Research from 97 B2B Websites and 29M visits
tldr: New data on how visitors arriving from AI search engines actually convert across 97 B2B sites. Rare hard numbers on the AI-referral traffic everyone's speculating about.
why_fresh: new original research on AI traffic
angle: What AI-search conversion data really means for content ROI planning.

title: Old Navy's MrBeast deal boosts engagement amid bigger bet on creators
tldr: Old Navy's MrBeast back-to-school campaign shows early traffic gains as Gap rewires marketing around creators. A concrete creator-partnership case study with early metrics.
why_fresh: fresh campaign case with early results
angle: When mega-creator deals actually move metrics — and when they don't.

title: The myth of the changing consumer
tldr: Argues that 'consumers have changed' is a lazy trend narrative — always look for the context behind the behavior. A useful corrective for anyone chasing consumption trends.
angle: Why 'the consumer has changed' is usually the wrong story — and what to ask instead.

title: Why you still aren't being taken seriously in the boardroom
tldr: Comms pros drown execs in analytics but fail to translate data into a story leadership cares about. A pointed take on the data-storytelling gap in communications.
angle: Turning comms metrics into a boardroom narrative execs actually feel.

title: Cracking GEO: How Smart Brevity Wins With Human and Machine Audiences
tldr: Argues AI is now the first reader of everything you publish, so brevity and structure must serve both humans and machines. A practical frame for writing in the GEO era.
angle: Writing for two readers at once: the human and the machine that ranks you.

title: Inside The Questlove Music Lab: A New Platform for Brand Storytelling
tldr: iHeartMedia launches a Questlove-led music lab as a brand storytelling platform, blending culture, audio and partnerships. A fresh owned-media format experiment.
angle: Culture-led owned media: what brands can learn from a Questlove music lab.

title: Портфельная карьера: что это и почему к ней придут все
tldr: On the rise of the portfolio career — juggling multiple projects without burnout instead of relying on one salary. Relevant to the creator-economy work model.
angle: The portfolio career as the default model for content professionals.

title: The campaign calendar is dead
tldr: Argues the fixed campaign calendar is obsolete in an always-on, reactive content environment. A provocation for editorial planning and ops.
angle: What replaces the editorial calendar when content goes always-on.

title: As AI reshapes newsrooms, leading media outlets are charting different paths for its use
tldr: Compares how major outlets are adopting (or resisting) generative AI in editorial work, from headlines to photo descriptions. Useful map of divergent AI-in-content policies.
angle: What newsroom AI policies reveal about governing AI in any content team.

title: Julie Seal: I think you are all too chicken to admit this AI ad is great
tldr: A contrarian defense of a well-made AI-generated ad, challenging the reflexive backlash against synthetic creative. Sharpens the human-vs-AI craft debate.
angle: When is an AI ad actually good? A framework beyond the reflexive backlash.

title: Bots Don't Click -- So What Will The Internet's New Business Model Be?
tldr: With AI agents browsing instead of humans clicking, the click-based ad economy faces an existential rethink. Big-picture on how content gets funded next.
angle: If bots browse and humans don't click, who pays for content?
